articles.title: 10 little habits inflating your grocery bill — and how to fix them
articles.summary: With everyone feeling the pinch, we asked experts for some practical solutions to the bad habits that can increase your grocery bill.
articles.body:
If rising grocery prices are changing how you shop, you're not alone.

In a June Omnisend survey of 1,075 consumers, 30% of respondents said they used a credit card to pay for essentials , such as groceries, knowing they might not pay off their bill.

Additionally, nearly 1 in 5 adults paid for groceries with savings, and nearly 1 in 20 bought groceries with cash from a payday advance loan, according to the Urban Institute Well-Being and Basic Needs Survey for 2025, which came out in July.

With everyone feeling the pinch, we asked experts for some practical, reality-based solutions to the bad habits that can increase your grocery bill. Avoid these mistakes and you may see big savings at the checkout line.

'There's no joy in living this way.' Families struggling to make ends meet

This is something every expert we spoke with mentioned as a problem for anyone sticking to a budget. Basically, it's the top mistake people make: heading into a store without a plan for shopping and a list in hand, be it written or on your phone. Take the extra step of evaluating what's on hand, how many meals need to be made, and what's realistic is critical to reducing your extra spending, explained Jenn Lueke , author of "Don't Think About Dinner ."

"Sitting down and making a plan, plus writing out the corresponding grocery list, allows you to choose meals with overlapping ingredients so the list is shorter and to make sure you're not shopping for an ingredient you already have in the back of the fridge," said Lueke.

Even having a loose plan for your week will reduce the amount of random items you add to your cart.

"Beyond that, having a plan and an efficient list will also prevent food waste, which is another way to save money," Lueke added.

2. Shopping when you're stressed, tired or hungry

All three of these, plus feeling under-the-weather, are what Dr. Lily Kaufmann, a licensed clinical psychologist , calls vulnerability factors. And she says to be careful about shopping when those factors are high.

"When vulnerability factors are high, we're also less able to access executive functioning skills, such as planning, organizing, and impulse control," Kaufmann said.

And lack of planning and impulse control, Kaufmann said, "can easily lead to overspending, buying things you don't need, abandoning health goals, or other shopping impulses you might regret later."

Shoppers can easily overspend, buy things they don't need or abandon health goals when their planning and organization skills are compromised, explained Kaufmann.

Steer clear of shopping whenever you're run down.

"While it could be helpful to get a treat to self-soothe, being tired or stressed makes it harder to consider your options and arrive at an intentional, thought-out decision," Kaufman said.

Most of us know the feeling of making a list and ending up at the register with a cart full of goodies that we probably don't need and definitely increased the bill. Prisca Benson, Money Coach at Our Green Life , said the solution is to send someone else (this also works if you're tired or stressed).

"Grocery pickup is a great option, but not everyone likes that due to increased cost, and being unsure of quality. A great alternative is creating the list and having someone else do the shopping who isn't tempted to grab things off the list. Personally, I send my husband to Costco and it has saved us so much money," said Benson.

We love convenience, but convenience will cost you money at the grocery store, where pre-chopped, pre-cooked or even pre-portioned items will increase your grocery spend.

Lueke said she's all for doing what you need to save energy, so if buying pre-cut or pre-made items is the thing that will prevent a mid-week takeout order, do what you need to do.

However, she said, a little extra effort goes a long way.

"If you're really focusing on cutting costs, buy whole fruits and vegetables, avoid pre-made sauces and marinades, and don't pick up pre-portioned snacks. Instead, take some time right when you get back from the grocery store to do that preparation," she said.

Emergencies come up, of course, but ask yourself if you really need to run to the store for an item, or can you make a swap?

Lueke said that the more times you enter a grocery store during the week, the more money you are going to spend.

"If you can limit your grocery shopping to just once a week, you're less likely to spend money on extras while you're shopping," she said.

Make a list, have a meal plan, and you can get everything you need for the entire week in one shop.

"Not only will you save money, but you'll also save time and energy too," Lueke said.

6. Skipping a pantry sweep before you shop

Ever go to the market, buy a pantry staple like flour or rice wine vinegar, only to get home and realize you had some stashed at the back of a cupboard?

You're not alone, but it's a money waster, according to Christina Musgrave, cookbook author and food blogger .

"Check your pantry for hidden grains such as rice, pasta, quinoa or baking items like chia seeds, vanilla or flours. We often buy these items and they get hidden, resulting in an unnecessary purchase," Musgrave said.

7. Ignoring grocery store sales when planning

You've checked your pantry, come up with an outline of meal plans, and put together a list, but what many of us forget is to check for sales while making a list. Letting those sales inform your shopping can make a big difference, Musgrave said.

"See if there are any sales you can work into your weekly meal plan, and check your freezer space to see if there's anything you can take advantage of stocking up on!" she said.

8. Thinking small when it comes to proteins

Buying in bulk differs depending on your family size, but buying meat and fish in large quantities is often a great way to cut back on spending.

"I love buying whole filets of salmon and making multiple meals. I can make baked Greek salmon, salmon and avocado rice bowls, and a BLT salmon salad, that's three different meals with the same protein," Musgrave said.

Buying a whole bird, like chicken or turkey, can also easily make two meals and even a delicious bone broth.

Beyond shopping sales, many grocers big and small offer either a loyalty card or an app with a loyalty program.

When you're checking out, ask your local grocer if they have a loyalty or rewards program and whether they offer personalized deals through their mobile app or in-store kiosks, said Ravi Achanta, CEO of RSA America . Also, depending on where you shop, your grocer may offer fuel rewards, which will help you save at the gas pump.

"Before you check out, take a minute to check your store's mobile app, loyalty account or kiosk for digital coupons and personalized offers you may need to activate," said Achanta.

This one goes back to planning, of course.

The U.S. Department of Agriculture reports that Americans waste 30% to 40% of their food every year, said Michael McAuliffe, president and founder of Family Credit Management .

"If you think about how often you buy food you don't use or don't eat leftovers you have, you'll start to see how so much food gets wasted. Think about just how much money you could save every month if you ate all the food you paid for," said McAuliffe.

Before you make your next trip to the grocery store, be sure to plan carefully, avoid overshopping and eat your leftovers!

articles.title: 'Congress is Bhasmasur': Rijiju hits back at Rahul Gandhi over 'party breaking' charge
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: Union minister Kiren Rijiju hit back at the Congress over its allegations that the BJP breaks other political parties, saying the charge sh.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Union minister Kiren Rijiju hit back at the Congress over its allegations that the BJP breaks other political parties, saying the charge should instead be directed at the Congress itself."What Rahul Gandhi and Congress should be saying for themselves is what they are saying for the BJP. Congress party is the 'Bhasmasur' which burns to ashes every party that comes into contact with them...TMC had emerged out of the Congress party. NCP had emerged out of the Congress party. Congress is accusing us but they themselves had broken out of another party. So, it is the Congress that breaks and burns other parties," Rijiju said.Rijiju said the BJP's growth under Prime Minister Narendra Modi had not involved breaking another political party."Under the leadership of PM Narendra Modi, BJP has emerged as the world's largest party but that didn't happen by breaking any other party. We do not play dirty like the Congress," he said.The development comes after the Election Commission on Friday allotted the Mamata Banerjee-led faction the name "Mamata All India Trinamool Congress" and the "Football Player" symbol. The rival faction led by Arup Roy was allotted the name "Democratic Trinamool Congress" and the "Envelope" symbol.The ECI issued the order under Article 324 of the Constitution and Paragraph 15 of the Election Symbols (Reservation & Allotment) Order, 1968, in Dispute Case No. 01 of 2026 involving the two rival factions.Pending the final determination of the dispute, neither the faction led by Arup Roy, the petitioner, nor the faction led by Mamata Banerjee, the respondent, has been permitted to use the original party name "All India Trinamool Congress" or the reserved "Flowers & Grass" symbol.Rahul Gandhi had criticised the move, alleging a pattern of the BJP and the Election Commission working together to split political parties and take away their election symbols."First Shiv Sena, then NCP, and now Trinamool Congress. Every time, the same pattern—BJP and the Election Commission join forces to split a party. Then its election symbol is snatched away," the Congress leader said."When an entire party can be stolen, it's hardly surprising that the votes of millions of Indians can be stolen too," he added.Following the ECI order, Mamata Banerjee termed the move unconstitutional and alleged that it was driven by political vendetta.Reacting to the freeze on the original party name and the "Flowers & Grass" symbol, Banerjee said, "We don't disrespect the Constitutional Chair, but we feel today is a black day in our democratic history. What is happening in our country is very unfortunate, unconstitutional, illegal, undemocratic and a totally biased vendetta to satisfy the ego of a political party."Banerjee also announced that her TMC faction would extend support to the Congress in the Nandigram bypoll, saying the decision had been taken in the "greater interest of the nation".Following the announcement, Sanchita Pradhan, the faction's candidate from the Nandigram Assembly constituency, withdrew her nomination, leaving the faction without a candidate in the seat ahead of the October 6 polling.The Congress has fielded Milan Pradhan from Nandigram, while the CPI has nominated Shanti Gopal Giri. The BJP's Hasirani Rath is also contesting the bypoll.The Nandigram seat fell vacant after Suvendu Adhikari gave up the constituency and chose to retain Bhabanipur, where he defeated Mamata Banerjee in the 2026 Assembly elections.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: QB Drake Maye and wife Ann Michael paid the classroom wish lists of all 54 teachers and support specialists at a Providence school where 98% of students get free or reduced-price lunch
articles.summary: US News: New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye and his wife, Ann Michael, have paid for the classroom wish lists of all 54 teachers and support specialis.
articles.body: New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye and his wife, Ann Michael, have paid for the classroom wish lists of all 54 teachers and support specialists at Alfred Lima Sr. Elementary School in Providence, Rhode Island. The donation was made through their nonprofit, the MayeDay Family Foundation, as the school prepared for the new academic year.According to WPRI 12, the surprise began with an email sent to Tonya Costa, principal of Alfred Lima Sr. Elementary School. Costa was preparing for her 26th year in the Providence Schools district when she received a message saying that someone was reaching out on behalf of Maye.At first, Costa was not sure whether the offer was genuine. She forwarded the message to her assistant vice principals, Kelli Goodwin and Elizabeth Melendez, before the three women looked into it and spoke with Maye."I'm not gonna lie, we were a little skeptical at first because we get a lot of emails. But we did a little research and talked to him and we realized it was real," Costa said, as quoted by WPRI 12.Once the school confirmed the offer, the Mayes worked with the staff to decide how they could help. They eventually agreed to cover the Amazon classroom wish lists of all 54 teachers and support specialists at the school.The gift was then turned into a surprise for the educators. Costa, Goodwin and Melendez called the teachers and support staff to what they described as an emergency meeting. Instead of an emergency, the staff were told that the Mayes had agreed to pay for their classroom supplies. "It was amazing," Costa said. "There were teachers crying. They couldn't have been more thankful."Donation supports a Title I schoolThe donation is particularly significant for Alfred Lima Sr. Elementary School because it is a Title I school. Such schools receive federal financial assistance through the US Department of Education because they serve a high percentage of children from low-income families.Costa said about 98% of the school's students receive free or reduced-price lunch. The school also has more than 400 multilingual learners, meaning those students speak Spanish or another language as their first language."Our school is a Title I school. So, 98% of our kids get free or reduced lunch. We have more than 400 multilingual learners, which means 400 of our students speak Spanish or another language as their first language. This provides them the opportunity to get special supplies for the kids in their classrooms that they wouldn't have otherwise," Costa said. The Mayes donated $15,000 in gift cards to the school to cover the cost of the 54 classroom wish lists.Tasha White, a library media specialist at Alfred Lima, said teachers often use their own money to purchase classroom necessities. "Most teachers have to take money out of their own pockets to buy a variety of supplies that are really necessities in the classroom," White said. "We are just so thankful for their generosity and for looking out for us."White said the donation would also give educators the opportunity to purchase supplies beyond the basic necessities. She described some of these as "luxury" supplies that could be used to enhance learning. "It's a wonderful feeling," White said. "We now have the chance to do things we otherwise wouldn't have been able to do."Teachers learn about surprise donationFor the educators, the announcement came without warning. Kristen Ayotte, a third-grade teacher at Alfred Lima, said she was especially excited about the donation because she is a Patriots fan."I am a big Patriots fan, so to tell my students and my own children that I was receiving a donation to purchase supplies for my classroom was super exciting," Ayotte said.The MayeDay Family Foundation was launched by Maye in March. Its first activation was a celebrity softball classic held at Polar Park in Worcester, Massachusetts, in May. The event raised more than $500,000 to benefit children and families in need in New England and North Carolina.Maye later spoke about the Providence school donation after practice on Wednesday. He said his wife was the person behind the idea for the gift. "In our light, we have been blessed by the lord and in what we have been given and we're trying to share it with others," Maye said.The school is now planning another event connected to the donation. Staff members want to invite the Mayes to Alfred Lima for a "Maye Day" in May, giving educators an opportunity to thank the couple in person.Goodwin said the gesture has continued to affect the staff. "Every time we talk about it it gives me goosebumps," she said.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Oxford United apologises for United 93 shirt advert
articles.summary: Oxford United apologises for the image, which features the call sign of one of the planes used in the 9/11 attacks.
articles.body:
A football club has apologised after it published images of a new clothing line with "United 93" printed on the back - the call sign of one of the aircraft hijacked on 9/11.

The clothing was supposed to make reference to Oxford United's founding year of 1893.

However, it said it had been released "without understanding of the historical context and associations".

United Airlines Flight 93 crashed in Shanksville, Pennsylvania, killing all 44 people on board after being hijacked on 11 September 2001. A docudrama film titled United 93 was made about the tragedy and released in 2006.

Oxford United was founded in 1893 as an amateur club called Headington and now plays in League One - the third tier of the English football pyramid.

In a statement, the club said its Campus Clothing range had been withdrawn and it "sincerely apologised" for the error.

"It should not have reached the point of sale and we take full responsibility for not undertaking proper due diligence," it said.

"We have removed the collection with immediate effect and are reviewing our approval processes to ensure nothing like this happens again."

The 9/11 attacks saw 19 Al Qaeda members hijack four commercial passenger planes in the US.

Two of them were flown into the Twin Towers of the World Trade Center in New York City, resulting in them both collapsing.

Another plane struck the Pentagon, near Washington DC, while the fourth plane - United 93 - crashed in rural Pennsylvania. It was believed to be destined for the US Capitol Building, also in Washington DC.

The attacks killed 2,977 people and injured tens of thousands more.

articles.title: California black jaguar Samba dies after venomous rattlesnake bite in Dunlap despite emergency antivenom treatment
articles.summary: US News: A black jaguar named Samba at Project Survival's Cat Haven, a wild cat conservation facility in Dunlap, California, has died following a venomous snak.
articles.body: A black jaguar named Samba at Project Survival's Cat Haven, a wild cat conservation facility in Dunlap, California, has died following a venomous snake bite. The 14-year-old jaguar, born at the sanctuary, was rushed for emergency veterinary care after staff noticed swelling in one leg. Despite receiving antivenom and showing signs of recovery, Samba died during the recovery process. Her death has drawn wider attention as California faces an unusually active rattlesnake season. Here's what happened, and what it says about the risks animals and people are facing this year.What happened to Samba the black jaguar at Cat HavenStaff at Project Survival's Cat Haven first suspected a problem when Samba remained in her den rather than coming out as usual. As sanctuary founder Dale Anderson told ABC News 4, staff then noticed her left paw had swollen to roughly twice the size of her right one, with the swelling extending up her leg. Samba was taken to the Fresno Veterinary Specialty & Emergency Center, where veterinarians anaesthetised her and administered two doses of antivenom. Testing had confirmed she had been envenomated, and this marked the second such bite involving one of the sanctuary's cats this year.Samba's death during recovery from treatmentTreatment initially appeared to be working, Anderson said the venom level in Samba's system fell to nearly zero following the antivenom doses. However, she died while veterinary staff were attempting to bring her out of anaesthesia during the recovery process. Hours after treatment began, Samba's heart stopped, and staff performed chest compressions and administered medication in an effort to revive her, without success. Anderson, who called Samba one of his own, described her as a sweet, calm and pleasant cat by personality. To determine whether any underlying health issues contributed to her death, her body was sent to the UC Davis California Animal Health and Food Safety Laboratory for a necropsy.A dangerous rattlesnake season across CaliforniaSamba's death comes amid what has been described as an especially dangerous rattlesnake season statewide. According to The Cool Down, the California Poison Control System had recorded 277 rattlesnake bites at the time of reporting, within the typical seasonal range of roughly 290 to 390 bites recorded annually between April and October. Anderson told reporters that rattlesnake activity on the sanctuary's 93-acre grounds has increased this year, with at least six of its cats treated for rattlesnake bites, all of which recovered after receiving antivenom. Experts have linked the rise in encounters to an unusually warm start to the year, which drew both snakes and people outdoors earlier than usual.How Cat Haven is responding to increased snake activityAs a wildlife conservation facility, Cat Haven takes a non-lethal approach to snakes found on its property. Anderson has also said staff do not want to kill snakes simply because they live on the grounds, and instead catch and relocate them elsewhere on site, away from the big cats; around 14 snakes have been moved this way so far this year. With mild weather bringing snakes out of hibernation earlier and increasing the chances of encounters with both people and animals, Samba's death is being viewed as part of a wider pattern of increasingly risky wildlife encounters this season.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: California approved $5 million toward buying 357 coastal acres once home to America's largest abalone farm; the $18 million tribal acquisition could revive aquaculture and restore habitat
articles.summary: US News: California has approved $5 million towards the purchase of 357 coastal acres in Cayucos that once housed the largest abalone farm in the US. The yak t.
articles.body: California has approved $5 million towards the purchase of 357 coastal acres in Cayucos that once housed the largest abalone farm in the US. The yak titʸu titʸu yak tiłhini Northern Chumash Tribe is seeking to buy the property for $18 million and restore parts of the land and its former aquaculture operation.According to The Tribune, the property, known as Alexander Ranch, has about one mile of coastline. It includes a eucalyptus grove that provides monarch butterfly habitat, a seasonal creek flowing into the Estero Bluffs and hills covered with grasses, sage and willow trees.The tribe's nonprofit organisation entered into a purchase agreement with the estate of engineer John Alexander in 2024. The fundraising deadline is October 15, when the escrow period ends. As of June 2026, the organisation had raised almost $8.2 million, including a $7 million grant from California's Sustainable Agricultural Lands Conservation Program.According to Becca Lucas Thomas, executive director of the ytt Northern Chumash Nonprofit, the land has a long connection with her people. Before Alexander used the property for aquaculture, it was home to an Indigenous village called tsitxala. The tribe had harvested abalone from the coast for thousands of years.“This property is really special. It holds a lot of history. To have the opportunity to bring this place back to our families today is really remarkable," Thomas says, as quoted by The Tribune.Tribe plans restoration workIf the purchase goes through, the tribe plans to manage the property using indigenous stewardship practices. The proposed restoration work includes repairing habitats in the Villa Creek watershed, with the aim of supporting the return of steelhead trout.The project is called yatspasini wa yaktspu Conservancy, meaning 'Ocean to land conservancy'. Lucas Thomas saysthe landscape had been actively managed by indigenous people before colonists forcibly removed them.The tribe historically transplanted selected plant species, maintained waterways and used intentional burning to manage the landscape.“While we look at this beautiful coastline, remember that it looks this way intentionally. It was created by our ancestors,” Thomas says.The property also offers a place for the tribe to reconnect with its ancestral land. Thomas says members could eventually gather and camp there without having to seek permission from another landowner or rent a campsite.Former abalone farm could reopenThe property also contains the remains of an abalone farm built during the 1960s. At its peak, the farm raised about 1 million abalone each year for meat.The facility closed in 2020. About 900 concrete aquaculture tanks have remained unused since then. The Harmony Coast Aquaculture Institute currently leases the facility and wants to work with the tribe on bringing the farm back into operation.Ben Ruttenberg, co-founder of the Harmony Coast Aquaculture Institute and director of Cal Poly's Center for Coastal Marine Sciences, said of ytt Tribe, "They are the perfect partner. This was originally their land.”The institute also holds a state permit for the farm's seawater intake pipe. According to Ruttenberg, the pipe can bring in about 7,000 gallons of seawater per minute. He said such permits are very difficult to obtain and are important for an aquaculture operation.The proposed system would use algae as part of the water treatment process. Seawater would first be pumped into an algae tank, where the algae would absorb nutrients. This would lower the water's carbon content and acidity before it reaches the abalone tanks.That is important because abalone build their calcium carbonate shells more effectively in less acidic water. The farm could also use the algae as food for the abalone. The animals need large amounts of food and can take about five years to reach market size.After passing through the abalone tanks, the water would have higher carbon content and acidity because of the animals' waste. It would therefore pass through another algae tank before being released back into the ocean.“Our goal here is to produce excellent water that is better than the water we brought in, or at least cleaner and has less carbon dioxide than the water we pumped in,” Ruttenberg said.Farm could support abalone restorationThe planned operation would not only focus on producing abalone for food. The tribe also hopes to use part of the facility for research and restoration.The former farm raised red abalone. Lucas Thomas said the tribe hopes to continue raising red abalone while also working with endangered white and black abalone for restoration.Black abalone are different from other abalone because they live in the intertidal zone. This is the part of the coast that is covered by the ocean during high tide and exposed to air during low tide. Other abalone species live in deeper water.Tribal members recently surveying the property found black abalone along the coastline. Lucas Thomas said that could make the property a useful location for black abalone restoration work.Scientists already understand how to raise white abalone in captivity and move them into the wild. However, there have been few successful attempts to raise black abalone on a farm.Lucas Thomas said some of the existing aquaculture facility could be used to study how black abalone can be raised in captivity.The project also has a cultural importance for the tribe because abalone has long been an important food source. California closed the recreational abalone fishery, while buying the molluscs has become expensive, leaving the tribe without consistent access to them.“Many of our elders grew up with abalone being a fixture,” Lucas Thomas said. “That just hasn’t been a thing for 30, 40 years.”Tribal members eat abalone and also use its shells to make jewellery and decorate regalia.“To be able to have access not only back and steady, but within our control, as something that we’d be able to provide directly for our community. It’s a really, really important piece of this for us,” Lucas Thomas said.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.summary: Maye Musk defended Sydney Sweeney's nude sports ad and slammed tax dollars sent to fake nursing homes in a wide-ranging interview with Tomi Lahren.
articles.body: Maye Musk, swimsuit model and mother of Elon Musk, joined OutKick’s "Tomi Lahren Is Fearless" to tackle Sydney Sweeney, government fraud, and her 18 grandkids. Musk jumped into defending Sydney Sweeney after the actress caught online heat over going nude for a sports ad. Lahren noted that Musk, who famously graced the Sports Illustrated Swimsuit cover at age 74, knows a thing or two about the industry. SYDNEY SWEENEY FIRES BACK AT TROLLS AFTER FACING CRITICISM ONLINE FOR PROVOCATIVE SPORTS AD "She’s a model," Musk told Tomi. "Well, she’s an actress, but she’s a model and modeling, you can look sexy and acting, you can look sexy and have fun." "I think she’s fabulous," Musk added. "I mean beautiful, fabulous and she seems to have a great sense of humor. So she’ll need it." To Maye, women can use their looks to build massive careers and have fun without taking a lecture from progressives. articles.title: Parents given only 2 months stay at Miami POE: Immigration attorney explains why a B1/B2 visa does not guarantee six months' stay in US
articles.summary: US News: A US visitor's visa allows a six-month stay during any single visit but that does not guarantee that they can remain in the US for six months. They wi.
articles.body: A US visitor's visa allows a six-month stay during any single visit but that does not guarantee that they can remain in the US for six months. They will have to follow the date that border officials give on the I-94 at the time of entry. Form I-94 is the US government's official arrival/departure record for most foreign nationals entering the US and it determines how long they are allowed to stay in the US.Recently, an NRI account posted on social media that the parents came to the US with their return tickets booked in February 2027 but at the Miami port of entry, the officers allowed them to stay only till November 2026, which would make the duration of their stay only two months. The NRI account said that the parents came for the birth of their grandchild, but if they have to leave in November, they would miss the birth. The account also said that the CBP officer noticed that the father had a job in India and hence asked why the parents needed a five-month stay in the US.Read: Parents came to US for 5 months, officer allowed only 2 months as father has a job in India: NRI shares parents' entry experience, seeks adviceWhile the NRI account sought advice on whether the parents could stay in the US until their visa expires or only until the date given on Form I-94, immigration attorney Gnanamookan Senthurjothi said this is a common misconception.B1/B2 visa does not guarantee a six-month staySenthurjothi said that the CBP determines the period of admission based on the circumstances of the individual traveller. It is common for the CBP to allow a six-month stay, but it is not guaranteed."CBP officers may consider factors such as the traveller’s stated purpose of visit, previous travel history, frequency and duration of prior stays, and other circumstances presented at the time of admission," the attorney said, explaining that in this particular case the parents can't stay in the US beyond the November date mentioned on the I-94 form. The expiration date printed on the visa is not the critical date here."If the purpose of the visit has been completed, leaving the US within the authorized period of admission is generally the safest course from an immigration-compliance perspective," he said.B1/B2 visa versus I-94The visa is a document in the passport while the I-94 is the electronic arrival/departure record. The visa is issued by the Department of State and the I-94 is issued by CBP.The B1/B2 visa allows one to travel to a US port of entry; it does not guarantee entry. CBP allows entry and the I-94's date determines the authorized stay.5 checklists for visitors on a B1/B2 visaSenthurjothi reminded that visa validity is not same as the authorized period of stay and the five things to remember are:A B1/B2 visa does not guarantee admission to the US.A B1/B2 visa does not guarantee a six-month I-94.CBP determines the authorized period of stay at the port of entry.Always check the I-94 after entering the US.The visa expiration date is not the date by which you must leave the US — the I-94 controls your authorized stay.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Meet Maya Penn: The young entrepreneur who turned $200 and handmade headbands into a $55,000 sustainable fashion business, giving 10% to charity
articles.summary: US News: At an age when most children were still figuring out what they wanted to do after school, Maya Penn was already making and selling her own accessories.
articles.body: At an age when most children were still figuring out what they wanted to do after school, Maya Penn was already making and selling her own accessories. The Atlanta youngster began with handmade headbands created from materials available at home, then gradually turned that small experiment into ‘Maya’s Ideas’, a business centred on clothing and accessories made with recycled and organic materials. By the time she was 12, Penn had attracted coverage from several major publications and television outlets, while her company was projected to generate about $55,000 in sales for the year., Penn planned to donate 10% of her profits to organisations in the Atlanta area.How Maya Penn started her sustainable fashion business at age eightPenn's first steps into business were fairly modest. At eight, she began making ribbon headbands for family friends, using fabric her mother already had around the house as well as pieces from recycled vintage clothing.In an interview with Entrepreneur in 2013, she shared that when she needed materials that were not available at home, her mother provided a budget of $200. Penn used that initial support to buy supplies, then put money from early sales back into the business. The operation grew from there rather than beginning with a large investment or formal commercial setup.The business eventually became ‘Maya’s Ideas’, an online shop offering handcrafted accessories and clothing. The materials she chose became an important part of how the company developed.How sustainability became part of Maya’s IdeasPenn's interest in environmental issues was influenced partly by her family. As mentioned in her interview, her father, John, was an entrepreneur who had explored solar energy as a child and had received awards for science fair projects connected with the subject from NASA and the US Air Force Honor Guard. Penn learned about environmental technology from him and later began investigating the materials used in her own products.That research led her to consider the effects of conventional clothing production, including the chemicals used in some textile dyes. Rather than treating environmental concerns as something separate from the business, she incorporated them into the products themselves.Maya’s Ideas consequently focused on accessories and clothing made with materials such as recycled fabrics and organic cotton. For Penn, the environmental element became part of the company's identity while she was still at school.Maya Penn’s family support helped turn her creativity into a businessThe family environment played a significant role in Penn's early business development. Her mother, Deidre, taught her how to sew, while her father's entrepreneurial background provided another example of running a business.The Penn family also homeschooled Maya, allowing her education to be shaped around areas including problem solving and developing creative ideas. Her parents encouraged her to make decisions for herself from a young age, with independence being treated as part of her development.That combination of practical skills, family support and room to experiment gave Penn the opportunity to test a business idea before she had reached her teenage years.From handmade products to tens of thousands in salesBy 2013, Maya’s Ideas was no longer simply a child's sewing project. Penn worked on the company part time alongside her studies and everyday life, yet the business was on course for approximately $55,000 in sales that year (2013).Penn's classmates were aware of what she was doing, too. She told Entrepreneur that some children found the business interesting and that some had been encouraged to consider starting ventures of their own.Maya Penn donated 10% of her business profits to Atlanta charitiesMaking money was not the only purpose Penn attached to the company. She had decided to give 10% of her profits to charities in the Atlanta area.The idea came from habits established at home. Penn had grown up accompanying her parents to buy food and canned goods for local food banks. Giving to people who needed assistance was therefore familiar to her before she started selling products.By the time of the 2013 interview, the profitable business had contributed $4,000 to charitable causes, alongside volunteer work.A young entrepreneur with several creative interestsPenn's activities extended beyond running an online shop. She was also described at the time as a designer, artist, animator, illustrator and writer, giving her business interests a much broader creative base than simply selling handmade accessories.Her early experience involved making physical products, but she was also interested in generating ideas, solving problems and communicating them. She encouraged other young people to keep track of their business ideas, including small thoughts that might eventually develop into something larger. Her own company had started in much the same way: with an experiment, some leftover fabric and a relatively small amount of money for additional supplies.Maya Penn took her sustainability message to TEDx and TEDPenn’s work soon moved beyond her own business. In November 2012, she documented a speech she gave at TEDx Youth, adding public speaking to the growing list of things she was doing as a young entrepreneur and environmental advocate.A year later, she appeared at TEDWomen 2013 with a talk titled ‘Meet a young entrepreneur, cartoonist, designer, activist’. TED describes Penn as having started her first company at eight and says the talk covered her approach to being responsible to both customers and the planet.The TED appearance also reflected the wider range of her interests. Alongside her fashion business, Penn was working in animation, illustration and environmental advocacy. Her TED profile now describes her as a three-time TED speaker and identifies her as the founder of a sustainable fashion company.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: ‘Fully compliant’: Nestlé India responds to FSSAI action over infant nutrition products
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Nestlé India on Friday said its infant nutrition products are fully compliant with applicable regulations, responding to legal action initi.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Nestlé India on Friday said its infant nutrition products are fully compliant with applicable regulations, responding to legal action initiated by the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) over promotional claims and other alleged violations involving three products.A Nestlé India spokesperson said NAN EXCELLA PRO and LACTOGEN PRO, along with their labels, had been approved by an expert committee of FSSAI, adding that the company had submitted a detailed response to the regulator, news agency ANI reported.“Our products are fully compliant with all the applicable regulations. The said products (i.e., NAN EXCELLA PRO & LACTOGEN PRO) and their labels were approved by the expert committee of FSSAI,” the spokesperson said.“In response to the notice, we have again submitted our detailed response to the authorities regarding statements appearing on the label, which are factual in nature, and supported by scientific literature,” the spokesperson added.Nestlé India also said it adheres to regulatory requirements and would continue to cooperate with the food safety regulator, ANI reported.“We confirm to adherence of all regulations including all norms and label declarations as per applicable laws. We will continue to work closely and support FSSAI in its efforts towards consumer awareness,” the spokesperson said.The response came after FSSAI said it had initiated legal action against Nestlé India over alleged non-compliances relating to infant nutrition products.According to FSSAI, it examined NAN EXCELLA PRO Stage 1 and LACTOGEN PRO 1, along with promotional material available on e-commerce platforms.The regulator said it observed claims relating to “5 HMOs” and “Whey Protein” for NAN LACTOGEN PRO Stage 1, while LACTOGEN PRO 1 carried a claim that “Whey Protein” was easy to digest, ANI reported.FSSAI said it sought clarifications from the company and subsequently found the two products to be in contravention of Regulation 4(2) of the Food Safety and Standards (Foods for Infant Nutrition) Regulations, 2020, which restricts promotional claims or material intended to increase the sale of infant foods.It also cited Section 3 of the Infant Milk Substitutes, Feeding Bottles and Infant Foods Act, 1992, which prohibits the advertisement and promotion of infant foods.Separately, FSSAI said a sample of a follow-up formula manufactured by Nestlé India was found to be sub-standard with respect to Biotin content during laboratory analysis.The regulator said a referral laboratory also found that the sample did not conform to the prescribed Biotin requirement.FSSAI said three separate adjudication cases had been filed against Nestlé India in respect of the three products.(With agency inputs)You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.title: A 31-year-old California entrepreneur started a portable-toilet business in 2023 with one truck and 100 units; two years later, nearly 2,000 toilets and 12 trucks helped bring in $4.3 million in 2025
articles.summary: US News: Daniel Tom was 31 when he started Bay Area Sanitation in 2023 with one truck and 100 portable toilets. Two years later, his business had grown to near.
articles.body: Daniel Tom was 31 when he started Bay Area Sanitation in 2023 with one truck and 100 portable toilets. Two years later, his business had grown to nearly 2,000 toilets and a fleet of 12 vacuum pumper trucks serving events and work sites across the San Francisco Bay Area. The company brought in $3.1 million in 2024 and $4.3 million in 2025, according to documents reviewed by CNBC.Tom’s business rents portable toilets and also handles their maintenance. This includes weekly cleaning, restocking supplies and removing waste from the units. Each portable toilet can hold up to 60 gallons of waste, which is emptied using the company’s vacuum pumper trucks.The business became profitable within its first year. Tom says most of the company’s income now comes from long-term rentals, where customers pay recurring charges for the toilets and their weekly cleaning. Standard portable toilets start at $160 a month for long-term rentals, while short-term rentals for events generally cost between $239 and $399 per event.The work may not sound attractive to everyone, and Tom says he often gets disgusted reactions when he tells people what he does. But he says those reactions usually change when he explains how the business operates and how much revenue it generates. “When I tell people that I own a porta-potty business, I get a lot of disgusted looks,” Tom says as quoted by CNBC. “But once I explain to them the business model and the revenue, most of the time they get interested,” he adds.From part-time job to business ownerTom’s connection with the portable-toilet industry began while he was studying at San Jose State University. During his junior year, he was studying to become a physical education teacher when he took a part-time customer service job at a portable-toilet rental company.The job changed his plans. “I liked it so much that I decided to abandon teaching and dive in full-time after graduation,” Tom says. He then worked for seven years as a sales manager at Hanson & Fitch before deciding to start his own company.When Bay Area Sanitation began in 2023, Tom started with just one truck and 100 toilets. The company later expanded as the number of toilets available for rent increased. By 2025, it was managing nearly 2,000 units and had 12 trucks operating across the Bay Area.The company serves different types of customers. Its portable toilets are used at short-term outdoor events such as concerts, as well as at construction sites and public parks where toilets may be required for longer periods.Focus on long-term rentalsTom says he prefers long-term rentals because they provide recurring income. Customers who rent the toilets for longer periods also pay for regular cleaning services. "I like to focus on long-term rentals because it equals guaranteed recurring revenue for my business,” he says.Tom says the business has a net profit margin of around 22%. Labour is the company’s biggest expense. Its 19 employees account for about 30% of revenue in labour costs. Other expenses include fuel for the vacuum and delivery trucks, along with supplies such as toilet paper and paper towels.Starting such a business also requires significant upfront spending. Tom estimates that a rentable portable toilet can cost around $800, while a vacuum truck can cost about $160,000. He did not disclose how much he personally spent to launch Bay Area Sanitation, but said the average person might need roughly $250,000 to get started.An AI-proof businessTom sees an unusual contrast in running a sanitation business in the San Francisco Bay Area, which is home to major technology companies such as Google, Apple and Nvidia.As artificial intelligence changes many types of work, Tom believes his business is based on a service that still requires people and physical work. “We’ve managed to build what I think is a low-tech, AI-proof business,” he says.He says he also takes pride in providing a service that people need. “The truth is, I take pride in what I do. I love coming to work every day and I provide a service that everybody needs. Everybody goes, right?”The business requires regular hands-on work. Tom says he has become used to the smell after cleaning many portable toilets, although some situations can still be difficult. “I’ve cleaned so many porta-potties the smell doesn’t really bother me,” he says. “But every once in a while, I’ll come across a unit after somebody’s had some bad burritos, or something like that. And even for me, it’s hard to stomach.”Plans to expand furtherTom says he is reinvesting most of the company’s profits rather than taking a larger personal income. His annual salary is around $120,000, but he says it could be higher if more of the profits were taken out of the business. “We’re really prioritizing reinvesting in the business to continue growing,” he says.His next target is to expand Bay Area Sanitation to 5,000 portable toilets and reach $10 million in annual revenue within the next five years. In December, the company signed a lease for a warehouse yard that has space for “almost twice as many trucks as we have now,” Tom says.The wider portable-toilet rental industry also has a sizeable market in the US. An IBISWorld analysis from September 2025 estimated that the industry generated $3.3 billion in 2025, up 1.7% from the previous year.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.summary: South Asia News: Bangladesh’s anti-graft agency said Friday it has sought details of the financial transactions of Asif Mahmud Shojib Bhuyain, a prominent leader of th.
articles.body: Bangladesh’s anti-graft agency said Friday it has sought details of the financial transactions of Asif Mahmud Shojib Bhuyain, a prominent leader of the 2024 “July Uprising” that ousted the Sheikh Hasina government, as part of a money-laundering investigation.Mahmud and his wife have been accused of laundering $1.05 billion during his tenure as an adviser in the Muhammad Yunus-led interim administration, which governed Bangladesh following Sheikh Hasina’s ouster. The Yunus-led administration stepped down after the February 12 elections, which were won by the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP).“We have asked the Financial Intelligence Unit to provide comprehensive information on the financial transactions and assets of Asif Mahmud Shojib Bhuyain and his wife,” an Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) spokesman told reporters, PTI reported.A key allegation against Bhuyain is that he was involved in laundering Taka 11,000 crore across five countries, including Taka 4,500 crore allegedly siphoned off to Dubai. He is also accused of using illicit funds to purchase land in Portugal.Bhuyain has said that, if found guilty, he would rather serve a prison sentence than flee the country.The ACC has reportedly received more than 2,000 written complaints against advisors and officials of the interim administration.ACC Secretary Saidur Rahman Khan previously denied allegations that Bhuyain was being deliberately targeted, saying the proceedings against him were being conducted strictly in accordance with the law.The anti-graft body launched its investigation on September 2 and has since obtained documents from the local government and youth ministries, which Bhuyain headed during the interim administration.Before leaving office, advisors to the interim government disclosed their wealth statements. articles.title: In 1979, Beach Boys co-founder Mike Love paid $435,000 for a 2.5-acre Lake Tahoe property; the nearly 19,000-sq-ft estate he built is now surrounded by six protected acres and listed for $43 million
articles.summary: US News: Beach Boys co-founder and lead singer Mike Love has listed his large Lake Tahoe estate for $43 million, ending more than four decades of family owners.
articles.body: Beach Boys co-founder and lead singer Mike Love has listed his large Lake Tahoe estate for $43 million, ending more than four decades of family ownership. The 83-year-old musician bought the 2.5-acre hillside property in 1979 for $435,000. Over the years, Love and his wife, Jacquelyne, built an 18,922-square-foot compound designed as both a private family home and a place for creative work. Located at 969 Fairview Boulevard in Incline Village on the Nevada side of the lake, the asking price is nearly 99 times what the couple originally paid for the undeveloped land.Built for privacy and creative workInstead of building directly on the busy lakefront, Love chose a higher site overlooking the water. This gave the family more privacy while providing wide views of Lake Tahoe and the Sierra Nevada. To protect the property from future development, the family bought six nearby acres and placed them under permanent conservation. This legal protection keeps the surrounding pine forest and rocky landscape from being developed, preserving the views and privacy. The home covers three levels and was built with stone taken directly from the property. For many years, it was Love's main creative workspace when he was not touring around the world. The mansion originally included a built-in recording studio with specially designed acoustic ceilings where Love wrote music. Although the studio has since been changed into a lounge and walk-in closet, the original acoustic features are still in place.Unique design and spiritual touchesThe estate includes unusual architectural and interior features influenced by Love's long practice of Transcendental Meditation and his interest in Eastern philosophy. Visitors enter through a stone archway and a 10-inch-thick front door. Love commissioned the solid wood door from temple craftsmen in southern India. It is decorated with rubies, diamonds and pearls and carved with an image of Ganesh. A temple priest also blessed the door. Inside the foyer, a spiral wrought-iron staircase rises above a koi pond. The area is covered by a hand-painted ceiling showing a celestial scene. The main living spaces have floor-to-ceiling windows and retractable walls that open onto large terraces. The main great room features a two-story river-rock fireplace, while the formal dining room can seat up to 14 people beneath crystal chandeliers. The compound has 10 bedrooms and 15 bathrooms. The main bedroom is located in its own private wing and includes a private deck and a cathedral-shaped headboard made from reclaimed wood.Resort-style features in a tax-friendly areaThe estate was designed for large family gatherings and includes many custom recreational and entertainment features. Inside, there is a professional chef's kitchen, a private movie theater with massage chairs and a popcorn station, a wine tasting room with a backlit agate ceiling, a poker room, an arcade, a boardroom, a gym, a cedar sauna and two elevators. Outside, the property has a swimming pool, a 10-person hot tub overlooking the lake, an outdoor kitchen with snow-melt decking, a trampoline and a custom ice-skating rink on the upper lawn. Listing agent Jeannette Harpole of Habitat Nevada at Keller Williams said the property offers a rare mix of privacy, protected natural surroundings and easy access to travel through the nearby Reno-Tahoe International Airport. Speaking to real estate outlet SFGATE about the protected surroundings, Harpole said: "There are views from every window, whether you're seeing Diamond Peak or you're seeing Lake Tahoe. It's majestic out there, and it's protected." The listing comes as ultra-luxury home sales have increased along the Nevada side of Lake Tahoe. Incline Village has attracted wealthy buyers partly because of Nevada's favorable tax system, which has no state income tax, corporate tax or capital gains tax. According to listing information published by Realtor.com and JamesEdition, Love and his wife are selling the longtime family home as their children have grown and the couple plans to spend more time travelling. The family also has strong ties to the North Shore community. They helped found the local Lake Tahoe School and supported the Incline Village Community Hospital.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: In 2001, Arthur Blank bought his first Montana guest ranch; 25 years later, his four properties span 33,000+ acres, including protected land and a Yellowstone River lodge opening to the public
articles.summary: US News: Home Depot co-founder and billionaire philanthropist Arthur Blank is expanding his business presence in Montana with a new public riverfront lodge, 25.
articles.body: Home Depot co-founder and billionaire philanthropist Arthur Blank is expanding his business presence in Montana with a new public riverfront lodge, 25 years after he bought his first guest ranch in the state. Through his holding company AMB West, Blank has developed a 6,000-acre riverfront property in Paradise Valley into Auster at Dome Mountain. The resort sits along the Yellowstone River and includes 20 year-round guest cabins, a main lodge, a casual restaurant, a rooftop bar and a retail market that is open to the public. The project marks a change for Blank, whose earlier ranch purchases in the area were mostly used for private family stays, company retreats, non-profit meetings and conservation work.25 years of growth in Paradise ValleyBlank entered Montana's real estate market in 2001 when he bought Mountain Sky Guest Ranch in Emigrant. Over the next 25 years, the businessman bought three more properties in Paradise Valley, building a portfolio that now covers more than 33,000 acres of owned and leased land. AMB West now manages four separate properties in the valley: Mountain Sky Guest Ranch, West Creek Ranch, Paradise Valley Ranch and Auster at Dome Mountain. Mountain Sky operates as a traditional luxury guest ranch. West Creek Ranch is mainly a private retreat and meeting place for non-profit groups supported by the Arthur M. Blank Family Foundation. Paradise Valley Ranch is mainly an agricultural operation, producing cattle and hay while following environmental protection practices. According to company information on the official AMB West website, all four properties are managed under one system focused on protecting the land, conservation and involvement in the southwest Montana community.Redeveloping a historic riverfront propertyBlank acquired the land for Auster at Dome Mountain in December 2021, when AMB West bought the former Dome Mountain Ranch. The 6,300-acre property is about 20 minutes north of the entrance to Yellowstone National Park. The new resort was built mainly within the existing footprint of the old 1960s guest ranch to reduce the impact on the surrounding landscape. Older guest cabins were moved and converted into housing for employees instead of being torn down. According to project information from the Arthur M. Blank Family Foundation and AMB West, the new property stretches along four and a half miles of the Yellowstone River. Guests can enjoy fishing, hiking, horseback riding and other outdoor activities. The name Auster comes from the Latin word for "south wind" and refers to the weather patterns that move through Paradise Valley. Company documents say the property was designed to be both a tourist destination and a public gathering place for local residents. The public areas, including the restaurant, coffee shop and retail market, will operate throughout the year and can be used without a resort reservation.Combining hospitality with wildlife protectionThe expansion comes as private land purchases across Montana continue to raise questions about public wildlife access and the breaking up of natural habitats. Paradise Valley is an important wildlife corridor for elk, grizzly bears, wolves and bighorn sheep moving out of Yellowstone National Park. AMB West says protecting the environment is a major focus of its properties. Much of its 33,000-acre network is covered by conservation easements, which limit large-scale commercial development and protect important winter habitat for local elk herds. In official documents about the property's environmental goals, AMB West stated: "AMB West properties are dedicated to protecting the natural environment and honoring local history through responsible stewardship, ensuring the land and its resources are preserved for future generations." Blank's foundation also uses the Montana properties for charitable programs. The foundation runs AMB West Basecamp at Mountain Sky, offering free facilities and meeting space to local and regional non-profit organizations. articles.title: Meet Harsh Jaiswal, Mohan Pedhapati and Rahul Maini: 3 Indian-origin researchers who used Claude to breach OpenAI systems, won $6,500 bounty
articles.summary: US News: Three Indian-origin cybersecurity researchers, Harsh Jaiswal, Mohan Pedhapati and Rahul Maini, demonstrated how Anthropic's Claude AI could be used to.
articles.body: Three Indian-origin cybersecurity researchers, Harsh Jaiswal, Mohan Pedhapati and Rahul Maini, demonstrated how Anthropic's Claude AI could be used to exploit vulnerabilities and gain access to OpenAI employee accounts and the company's internal code repository, Wall Street Journal reported.The researchers, who work at cybersecurity startup Hacktron AI, carried out the research in July 2026 while investigating security weaknesses at leading AI companies. They eventually chained two separate vulnerabilities to move from OpenAI's public community forum to employee ChatGPT and Codex accounts and then to an internal GitHub repository.The researchers said the entire chain, from their initial discovery to demonstrating access to OpenAI's internal repository, took less than 72 hours. They spent under $3,000 on AI tokens and won a bounty of $6,500 after they disclosed the issues to OpenAI.How did the researchers get into OpenAI's systems?The attack began at community.openai.com, OpenAI's community and help forum, which is operated using the third-party platform Discourse.Hacktron researchers discovered that specially crafted HEIC/HEIF image files could exploit a vulnerability in the image-processing software used by Discourse. The vulnerability was linked to the `libheif` image-decoding library and could allow remote code execution — essentially giving an attacker the ability to execute commands on the affected server.However, gaining control of the forum server alone did not provide direct access to OpenAI's internal code.To safely demonstrate proof of access without viewing sensitive IP or source code, they used a compromised employee's Codex account to submit a harmless pull request to OpenAI's internal private repositoryThey prominently used Anthropic's Claude AI models (spending under $3,000 in API tokens) to help write, debug, and port the binary exploits faster, showcasing how offensive AI capabilities accelerate vulnerability research.Then they reported the findings responsibly through Bugcrowd and HackerOne to OpenAI and Discourse. OpenAI patched the identity issue shortly after notification and awarded them a $6,500 bug bounty.In a statement to Forbes, OpenAI spokesperson Drew Pusateri said the company thanked the researchers “for contacting us and sharing their findings,” and noted that it had resolved the vulnerability.'No brand name, colleges or companies'Tech commentator Deedy Das pointed out that none of the three researchers had any big college name on their CVs. articles.title: Boca Raton council votes 3-2 to impose $100 minimum fine for feeding iguanas, rats, mice and pigeons under new Florida ordinance
articles.summary: US News: Boca Raton, Florida, has voted to make feeding iguanas and other nuisance animals a punishable offence. The city council passed a new ordinance by a n.
articles.body: Boca Raton, Florida, has voted to make feeding iguanas and other nuisance animals a punishable offence. The city council passed a new ordinance by a narrow 3-2 margin, introducing a $100 citation for anyone who feeds iguanas, rats, mice or pigeons in a way likely to draw or sustain large groups of them. Bird feeders and feral cats are excluded from the rule. Here's how the vote played out, and what officials on both sides had to say about it.What the new Boca Raton animal ordinance coversAs reported by CBS 12, the ordinance prohibits feeding iguanas, rats, mice or pigeons in a manner likely to attract or sustain large groups of them. Bird feeders and feral cats are specifically excluded from the rule, meaning the restriction is aimed at feeding behaviour that draws in or keeps nuisance animal populations rather than at feeding wildlife in general. Anyone found in violation of the ordinance faces a $100 citation. The rule now forms part of Boca Raton's municipal code following the council's vote.Boca Raton council votes 3-2; approves $100 iguana feeding fineThe Boca Raton City Council voted in a 3-2 majority to make feeding iguanas and other nuisance animals a code violation, carrying a penalty of a $100 citation. Mayor Andy Thomson, along with council members Jon Perlman and Stacy Sipple, voted in favour of both the ordinance and the fine. While the Deputy Mayor Michelle Grau and council member Yvette Drucker voted against it. This narrow split reflects genuine disagreement among council members over whether the issue warranted a formal code change at all.Why two council members opposed the $100 fineNot every council member supported the measure. Yvette Drucker argued that the ordinance would be difficult to enforce and questioned whether the issue was serious enough to be considered by the council. Deputy Mayor Michelle Grau also questioned its potential enforcement, while separately expressing concerns about unnecessary government regulation. Their objections centred less on the underlying problem of nuisance animal feeding and more on practicality and the appropriate scope of local government intervention, setting up the 3-2 split that ultimately passed the ordinance despite their reservations.Why the mayor defends the ordinanceIn defending the ordinance, Mayor Andy Thomson argued that addressing smaller issues affecting residents is also part of the council's responsibility, dispelling suggestions that the issue was not serious enough to warrant a rule change. His position, together with the votes of council members secured the ordinance's passage over the objections raised. The vote means Boca Raton now formally treats the feeding of iguanas and other nuisance animals as an enforceable code violation.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'Scream' star admits he's 'ashamed' of sequel return after actress fired over anti-Israel comments
articles.summary: Matthew Lillard says he feels "ashamed" for returning to "Scream 7" after Melissa Barrera's firing, calling himself on the "wrong side of history."
articles.body: "Scream" actor Matthew Lillard said Tuesday that he felt "ashamed" for returning to the horror franchise after actress Melissa Barrera was fired over social media posts about Israel and the war in Gaza, telling fans during a 30th anniversary screening in Austin, Texas, that he believed he ended up on the "wrong side of history." Lillard, who reprised his role as Stu Macher in the seventh installment, said his excitement about returning to the franchise overshadowed his concerns about how Barrera had been treated. As reported by Entertainment Weekly, Lillard said, "I went back to do ‘Scream,’ and I got called out. And I’m like, ‘Oh, f---. That’s brutal.’" "I feel bad about that. I feel ashamed about that. Because in that moment I was so excited to go back, I didn’t really think about Melissa and that journey." "I’m embarrassed, that’s the truth… I blew that. I’m on the wrong side of history for that. I still like being in the movie [but] it may not have been the best idea," Lillard continued. PEREZ HILTON JOINS 'TOMI LAHREN IS FEARLESS' AND DECLARES CANCEL CULTURE IS NOW A SPORT Barrera was dropped from the franchise in November 2023 after publishing and sharing a series of posts criticizing Israel following Hamas' Oct. 7 terrorist attack. In one post previously reported by Fox News Digital, Barrera accused Israel of committing "genocide" and "ethnic cleansing" in Gaza. "Gaza is currently being treated like a concentration camp," Barrera said. "Cornering everyone together, with no where to go, no electricity no water … People have [learned] nothing from our histories. And just like our histories, people are still silently watching it all happen. THIS IS GENOCIDE & ETHNIC CLEANSING." In another post, Barrera claimed Western news outlets were disproportionately presenting Israel's side of the conflict and told followers to draw their own conclusions about why. ‘NO JEWS, NO NEWS’ STRIKES AGAIN AS SELECTIVE COVERAGE OF THE 'UNSETTLERS' FUELS ANTI-ISRAEL ANGER "Because western media only shows the other side. Why they do that, I will let you deduce for yourself," Barrera said. Spyglass denied at the time that Barrera was removed merely for supporting Palestinians, instead saying it viewed some of her rhetoric as antisemitic. "Spyglass’ stance is unequivocally clear: We have zero tolerance for antisemitism or the incitement of hate in any form, including false references to genocide, ethnic cleansing, Holocaust distortion or anything that flagrantly crosses the line into hate speech," the company said. Fox News Digital reached out to Spyglass Media for comment about Lillard's remarks. Barrera subsequently rejected the suggestion that she was promoting antisemitism and defended her criticism of governments, Fox News Digital reported in May. MORE THAN 180 JEWISH ENTERTAINERS RALLY BEHIND ACTOR MARK RUFFALO IN PROTEST LETTER "I believe a group of people are not their leadership and that no governing body should be above criticism. I pray day and night for no more deaths, for no more violence and for peaceful co-existence," Barrera said. The controversy resurfaced earlier this year when Barrera criticized former cast-mates who returned to the franchise without her. When asked whether actors who went back for "Scream 7" were "scabby," Barrera agreed. "One hundred percent. I think they all are," Barrera said. "And they have to live with that." At Tuesday’s screening, Lillard directly defended Barrera’s position and criticized the lack of public support she received after her firing. "Melissa Barrera, who’s a beautiful actor, was fired for what she said after the whole Palestinian... what started happening in Israel," Lillard said. "It’s really f---ing bulls--- and really hard, and she’s on the right side of history." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "When that happened to Melissa, the whole world didn’t pipe up, but she was a year early on what the f---’s going on. But the whole world should have popped up and said, ‘She’s right.’ And they didn’t. And that’s brutal." Despite the upheaval surrounding its development, "Scream 7" was released Feb. 27 and eventually crossed $200 million at the global box office, becoming the highest-grossing film in the franchise’s history, according to Paramount. The film shifted its focus back to Neve Campbell’s Sidney Prescott and brought back several franchise veterans, including Lillard. When reached for comment by Fox News Digital, Hollywood in Toto editor Christian Toto said of Lillard’s remarks: "Now that the Palestinian cause is spiking in his far-Left industry, he has regrets. Now. Months after shooting the film. Months after its release. Months after the actress in question lost the role." Toto added, "Will he give all the money back? Does he know what she actually said about Israel and the timing of those comments? Is he aware of other artists who have had their free speech rights trampled?"

articles.title: Londonderry: Man admits to killing of Spanish national, court told
articles.summary: Ciaran Edward Murray, 30, of Malvern Terrace in Derry is charged with the murder of a 65-year-old Spanish national in 2024.
articles.body:
A man has admitted to killing a woman who was found dead in a ground-floor flat after a blaze at the property more than two years ago, a court has heard.

Ciaran Edward Murray, 30, of Malvern Terrace in the Waterside area of Londonderry, is charged with the murder of 65-year-old Spanish national Montserrat Martorell.

Her body was discovered in a flat in the Harvey Street area of Derry on 24 August 2024.

Appearing via video link before Belfast Crown Court on Friday, when the charge of murder was put to him, the 30-year-old replied: "Not guilty, but guilty to manslaughter."

Following this, prosecution lawyer told the court that his instructions were to proceed with the murder case.

A defence lawyer said a psychologist was due to examine the accused in late October.

They added that the defence had been instructed by the accused "at this first opportunity, to apologise to the family of the deceased for his actions".

Prosecution counsel Simon Reid KC said that, in light of the defence seeking a report from a clinical psychologist, he would have a clinical psychologist for the prosecution on standby once the defence report was delivered.

Mr Justice Fowler said he would list the case for November for an update on progress with the medical report.
